# Nicolas Lekai — AI Systems Architect

> Independent, vendor-neutral AI systems architect. Builds a company's own AI operating system: every model and tool it pays for in one place, all costs in view, a sidecar app for every role and a data tree of company knowledge that stays when the models change. Munich and London. The same person also works as a director for film, VFX and post-production at nicolaslekai.com. A two-minute explainer film (English and German) sits at the top of the page.

## What this is

Every day a company creates knowledge: in briefs and meetings, research, edits and campaigns. Today it is scattered across inboxes and chats, cloud accounts, hard drives, people's heads and a dozen AI tools that do not talk to each other. Nicolas Lekai starts with a five-day audit of how the work really flows, then builds the company's own AI operating system. It brings together everything the traditional software and the new AI tools can do; every model and software the company pays for runs under its hood. A small team of specialists runs it from the control centre and keeps it up to date in the background.

## The sidecar

Everyone else gets a sidecar: a small app shaped to their role. People write or speak in plain words and the AI does the rest, for example cutting today's interview to a 60-second 9:16 clip with subtitles, ready for review. It saves time every week on editing, design, motion graphics, transcripts, social media and planning on one timeline, while the creativity and the decisions stay with the people.

## Services

- AI operating systems — the company's own AI operating system with a control centre and a sidecar for everyone, plus internal tools shaped around how a team already works
- Production pipelines — AI image and video pipelines wired into real post-production, built by filmmakers and CGI artists with over 25 years of experience
- Strategy and training — audits, roadmaps and build-vs-buy calls with real numbers; hands-on training at the desk, role by role: easy to learn, fun to use

## All costs in view

The system meters every model and every tool the moment it runs (image, video, language, voice) and enforces hard budget caps per tool, per project and per month. All providers appear in one view: the month total, the spend per day and the spend per model.

## The data tree of company knowledge

Everything the company knows grows into one data tree: every project, decision and file, the brand voice, the skill files, the clients and the workflows. Everything in one place and everything connected. The models get better every year, even if the provider changes, from closed to open-weights models or vice versa; the tree stays the same and every model can keep tending it. Start collecting today, and you plant the tree the company will be tomorrow.

## Secure by design

Encrypted, locally and in the cloud. Everything the company makes stays in its own system, and the company decides what leaves it.

## How the work runs

- Phase 01, audit (about 5 days) — mapping the real workflows with the teams, ending in a written brief with the hours and the costs in it
- Phase 02, build (about 4 to 8 weeks) — the highest-value systems built in the company's own stack, shipped in weekly increments the client can veto
- Phase 03, train (ongoing) — training the people (easy to learn, fun to use), documenting everything, then stepping back; optional retainer as models change

## Tools under the hood

Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, Llama, Mistral, Whisper, ElevenLabs, ComfyUI, Flora, Higgsfield, Flux, Kling, Veo, Midjourney, DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, Houdini, Blender, Unreal, After Effects, Photoshop, Figma, Notion, Slack, WhatsApp, Gmail, Drive, Dropbox, Sheets, HubSpot, Stripe, GitHub.

## Position

Off-the-shelf AI makes every company equally average. These systems are built around the way a specific company works, so they cannot simply be subscribed to by a competitor. Nothing is resold: if the right answer is a small subscription rather than a platform migration, that is the recommendation. Scopes are fixed, demos weekly, and every initiative has kill criteria.
